# C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management

*Level 1 card. 5 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from thread/task misuse, synchronization overhead, contention, or failure to exploit available parallelism. This includes heavyweight or over-broad locking (excessive contention), architectural bottlenecks that force serial execution (serial bottleneck), threads or tasks that are never properly stopped (leaked threads), running heavy work on the main/UI thread (blocking main thread), and executing independent work serially when concurrency would reduce total time and energy (missed parallelism). In Python, the GIL makes threading ineffective for CPU-bound work; use multiprocessing for CPU-bound and asyncio/threading for I/O-bound tasks.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | a lock held across work that shares nothing, serialising what could overlap | hold the lock only over the shared state, or remove the need for it | yes, scales with input |
| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | concurrency paid for in full while one shared resource serialises all of it | give each worker its own resource, shard the work, or stop pretending to parallelise | yes, scales with input |
| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | workers started and never stopped, accumulating for the life of the process | give every worker a stopping condition, or reuse a bounded pool | yes, scales with call count |
| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | a synchronous blocking call inside a coroutine, stopping every other task | await the async equivalent, or move the blocking work off the loop | yes, scales with call count |
| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | independent work run one item at a time when the waits could have overlapped | run the independent work concurrently, with the tool the work's nature requires | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C11.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C11.S5.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
